job.title: Consultant, Risk Advisory
job.description:
Opportunity to get in early with a scaling Risk Advisory practice at one of Australia’s leading professional services firms. With a strong pipeline of client mandates, you’ll work on high-profile regulatory matters for tier-1 financial services clients, alongside industry-leading practitioners and specialists in risk, data and technology.

The Role

This fully integrated practice delivers a full suite of risk advisory services to global and domestic clients in the public and private sectors. With a strong pipeline of client mandates, the team is now looking for a Consultant ready to take the next step in their career.

You’ll work closely with senior practitioners on advisory engagements across risk management, regulatory and compliance matters, mostly for a portfolio of tier-1 financial services clients. You’ll help clients find their way through complex regulatory environments, manage risk well and meet their business goals. Many of these matters will shape markets and regulatory landscapes.

Key Responsibilities

  • Help design and implement risk management frameworks
  • Deliver regulatory compliance advice and governance reviews
  • Support work on regulatory enforcements and investigations
  • Contribute to strategic advice that is practical, innovative and commercially focused

Desired Experience

  • 1 to 3+ years’ consulting experience, ideally gained at a top-tier professional or financial services firm
  • Some familiarity with Australian regulatory frameworks, including APRA, ASIC and/or AUSTRAC
  • Tertiary qualifications in law, commerce, business or another relevant field, with excellent academic results
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Strong written and verbal communication, and confidence dealing with stakeholders at every level of seniority
  • An agile mindset, curiosity and a real enthusiasm for working in multidisciplinary teams

Benefits

  • Professional development programs and clear opportunities for career growth
  • First-class infrastructure, including access to leading AI platforms
  • Health and wellbeing initiatives that support both physical and mental health
  • A collaborative, inclusive culture that celebrates diversity
  • Up to 26 weeks’ paid parental leave, which can be taken flexibly over two years, with superannuation paid
  • The option to buy up to 4 weeks of extra leave each year
  • Flexible working arrangements are supported

How to Apply

If you’re ready to grow with a scaling practice and work on matters that shape the market, we want to hear from you. Apply now by submitting your CV for immediate consideration.

For a confidential chat, contact Jen Jones at Ink Recruitment on +61 (0)409 926 897.

job.title: Senior Manager, Credit Risk
job.description:
Step into a senior, strategic credit risk seat in a highly regarded financial institution. This is much more than credit assessments. You’ll help shape risk management across the whole State, with real exposure at committee and Board level.

The role will take the lead on driving successful credit risk outcomes and is one of three senior leaders seats sitting directly under the CRO.

The Role

You’ll lead the credit risk function for the organisation covering lending to corporate entities. Alongside the core credit work, you’ll contribute to a significant piece of risk management strategy within the broader business. The plan is for this person to move steadily away from the day-to-day and into strategy as the team grows in capability. Key responsibilities include:

  • Lead credit risk oversight across lending to complex corporate entities
  • Lead the internal executive Investment and Credit Committee, which oversees credit risk and the investment portfolios
  • Deliver credit assessments and annual credit reviews for the Board, and oversee corporate bond and investment management activity
  • Own credit risk policy reviews, along with the supporting monitoring and reporting
  • Contribute to broader risk management work and support engagement with rating agencies on the credit rating
  • Advise and report to the CRO and, under the CRO’s direction, to the Board, CEO and management committees
  • Watch the financial and operating environment for emerging risks and recommend action to protect the organisation’s position
  • Lead and develop a team of three

Desired Experience

  • Corporate, institutional or financial markets credit background (a retail credit background won’t suit this role)
  • Broader financial risk experience is welcome. You don’t need to be a credit guru, but you know what good credit oversight looks like
  • A strategic, commercially minded approach that goes beyond black-and-white quantitative analysis
  • People leadership experience, with a genuine interest in building up a developing team
  • Confidence working at committee level and presenting to the Board
  • Initiative and curiosity, the kind of person who does their homework and adds value beyond the brief
  • Ambitious Associate Directors who think strategically and are ready to step up are encouraged to apply

Benefits

  • Very stable organisation, with flexible working
  • Regular exposure to executive committees and the Board
  • A clear pathway from technical credit work into strategic risk leadership
  • A team to shape and develop

How to Apply

Candidates from interstate who are open to a move to Perth are very welcome. To apply, click Apply. For a confidential conversation, contact Jen Jones at jen.jones@inkrecruitment.com.au or on 0409926897.

job.title: Head of Assurance | Remediation Program
job.description:
The Role

Ink Recruitment has been engaged to recruit a Head of Assurance for a well-renowned, Sydney-based financial services organisation. Reporting to a member of the executive team and sitting on the program leadership team, you will provide independent second-line oversight across a critical remediation program, with accountability for assurance over remediation design, delivery, reconciliation, financial integrity and closure.

You will lead one direct report with support from a broader project team. This is a role for someone who brings independent judgement and constructive challenge, testing whether methodologies, controls and customer outcomes are working as intended and backed by complete, regulator-ready evidence, while keeping clear separation from the design and execution teams.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead independent assurance across solution design, operational delivery and program closure, with a risk-based assurance plan aligned to remediation priorities, material risks and regulatory expectations
  • Assess design and delivery of methodologies, treatment plans, population logic, calculations, processes and controls, and test that remediation is applied consistently across customer, claims, premium and payment outcomes
  • Oversee end-to-end reconciliation across populations, customer outcomes, claims, refunds, payments and financial records, ensuring exceptions and variances are investigated, resolved and evidenced
  • Evaluate control effectiveness across remediation processes and hand-offs, maintaining transparent findings and actions and confirming root causes are sustainably addressed
  • Define closure requirements and provide an independent view on whether outcomes, reconciliation, control actions and residual risk support workstream and program closure
  • Report with clarity to executive, Steering Committee, Board and Board committees, and support regulatory engagement with complete, consistent and defensible evidence
  • Lead and coordinate, managing your direct report and working with specialist support across Risk, Finance, Legal, Internal Audit and external advisers

Desired Experience

  • Banking or financial services background with strong audit or assurance experience
  • Working knowledge of remediation programs, ideally large-scale regulatory remediation
  • Proven track record designing and leading risk-based assurance across complex programs or operational processes
  • Strong reconciliation and financial integrity capability, including investigating and resolving exceptions and variances
  • Experience assessing control design and operating effectiveness and validating sustainable closure of findings
  • Confident Board, executive, audit and regulatory reporting, with clear and authoritative advice
  • Sharp analytical judgement, professional scepticism and the confidence to challenge senior stakeholders constructively
  • Tertiary qualification in risk, audit, finance, accounting, law, business or a related field, or equivalent senior experience
  • Availability to start ASAP

Benefits

  • High-visibility role with direct exposure to the Board and executive
  • Genuine independence and the mandate to shape assurance practice
  • Opportunity to embed lasting reconciliation, evidence and closure discipline across the organisation
  • Incredibly collaborative culture with supportive executives setting the right tone from the top
  • Up to $245,000 package. Remote or hybrid working available

How to Apply

If you bring independent judgement, rigour and a commitment to fair customer outcomes, we’d love to hear from you. Submit your CV to hello@inkrecruitment.com.au or apply via Seek below.

For a confidential chat, contact Jen Jones at Ink Recruitment on +61 (0)409 926 897.
